best_field_traits: Warm-season perennial grass often with a compact leafy base and delicate spreading flowering branches that form an airy loose panicle, at times detach and roll. Spikelets are small and terminal on long slender pedicels; long hairs at swollen branching axils and a wavily crimped whitish margin on one side of leaf blades can aid confirmation. Neither the source photos nor a Florida/PA occurrence certifies Hays County native status.
Perennial warm-season grass, with several slender, wiry often knotty stems emerging from a relatively horizontal, typically hairy basal crown.
Strongly open branched broomlike panicle, commonly up to about 30 cm long, widening substantially with maturity; mature panicle may detach and tumble.
Individual spikelets rather than tight rows along fingerlike branches; spikelets small, fuzzy/hairy, usually under about 3.3 mm.
Panicle branch nodes/axils often expanded or swollen and may show long radiating white hairs, useful as a high-value photo target.
Short relatively stiff flat blades often have a conspicuous pale, crinkled or wavy margin (one side can resemble a wavy saw). Do not call the species from this alone.
Plant color can shift pale green to straw/gold by fall; color alone is not diagnostic.
Formerly frequently treated as Leptoloma cognatum; ITIS and POWO accept Digitaria cognata, and this is not a second separate grass card.
crew_field_check: Use original and CC0 terminal-spikelet photos to see many individual oval spikelets separated by hair-fine stalks, NOT crowded onto fingerlike racemes.
Use the second CC0 habit photo for the leafy lower tuft, but do not infer a proven perennial base/root crown from one photo.
On the same plant find one swollen branch axil and photograph ACTUAL radiating hairs under 10–20×; these hairs are not independently verified in the current photos.
Check one blade's pale wavy/crinkled edge versus opposite edge with a 1-mm scale; the existing wide tuft picture is too distant to prove it.
Record ripe spikelet measurements and a correctly identified specimen before native county certification; Texas state-native listing does not certify Hays County.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole attached open panicle, full rooted perennial base and true flowering stalk photographed with cm ruler
Macro of a truly swollen branch node showing white axillary radiating hairs at 10–20×
One-side crimped pale leaf-blade margin next to the smoother opposite edge (same leaf), 1-mm reference
Mature single terminal oval spikelet face/side and attachment stalk with 1-mm scale; dorsal floret detail
True sheath–blade ligule and crown/base on documented Hays-area plant if photographed lawfully

comparisons.key_distinctions: Against D. ciliaris, there are NO fingerlike tightly paired spikelet racemes: the source photos show widely separated individually stalked units in a fragile branching broom. Other airy genera such as Panicum, Sporobolus and some Eragrostis can look similar; inspect the oval spikelet and actual leaf margin and hairy axillary swellings. Aristida has conspicuous three-parted true awns, absent on D. cognata. Its older Leptoloma cognatum name is a synonym, not a second card.

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.look_here_first: Fall witchgrass: follow the very open, airy, hair-fine panicle to individually stalked oval spikelets rather than fingerlike racemes. Confirm the perennial basal crown and inspect one mature spikelet plus the true membranous ligule; the swollen hairy branch junction and pale wavy leaf edge are supporting characters, not verified in existing pixels.

measurable_diagnostics.growth_form: Warm-season perennial with wiry, often branched culms and a persistent leafy basal crown; a detached seedhead cannot prove perennial habit.
measurable_diagnostics.ligule_collar: Membranous ligule approximately 0.2–1.5 mm (Go Botany); auricles absent. Photograph the actual blade–sheath junction at 1-mm scale, distinguishing any adjacent collar hairs.
measurable_diagnostics.flowering_architecture: Very open, diffuse panicle with isolated small spikelets on long fine pedicels; no tight fingerlike spikelet-bearing racemes. Axillary swollen branch nodes may carry white radiating hairs, requiring a real close-up.
measurable_diagnostics.spikelet_glumes: Awnless oval spikelets approximately 2.2–3.1 mm long; lower glume reduced to a small scale usually no more than 1 mm, upper glume approximately 1.8–2.8 mm and commonly 3–5-veined (Minnesota Wildflowers).
measurable_diagnostics.lemmas_florets_awns: One lower sterile and one upper fertile floret per spikelet. Lower sterile lemma commonly about spikelet length, roughly 7-veined; fertile lemma and palea firm, darkening at maturity. Neither true lemma nor glume bears a long awn. Do not count the two florets as two separate spikelets.

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.local_lookalikes: Panicum capillare is a robust hairy ANNUAL with diffuse panicle but a hair-fringe ligule; Eragrostis spectabilis has several fertile florets per spikelet and a different hairy ligule; Digitaria ciliaris has several fingerlike, one-sided racemes with paired spikelets, unlike the dispersed terminal units of D. cognata.
last_mile_photo_arrow_gaps: CONNECTED ROOT/BASE: covered by two source-identified collected specimens with visible fibrous roots and attached flowering axes. An in-situ Hays-area rooted habitat specimen/photo remains a separate gap; do not claim rhizome anatomy.
True exposed membranous ligule at opened blade/sheath junction with 1-mm bar; no new arrow until true inner free margin is resolved.
Three mature spikelets with 1-mm scale; isolate lower and upper glumes, lower sterile lemma, upper fertile lemma and palea under 10–20×, annotate only actual photographed separations.
True swollen panicle branch axil with radiating hairs and both blade margins on the same attached leaf.
Comparable maturity images of P. capillare and E. spectabilis reproductive and ligule characters under verified publication rights.

visual_comparison.overlay_note:
TEN real, source-attributed gallery panels use physically archived GitHub JPEGs: seven exact-species Digitaria cognata photos (indices 0–6; 18 gross-feature overlay arrows) and three clearly labelled different-species D. ciliaris look-alike panels (indices 7–9; 8 gross-feature arrows). The first two same-species photos now show physically connected fibrous roots, basal shoots and flowering culm. No photo yet clearly resolves the free inner membranous ligule (~0.5 mm in Texas key), swollen hairy panicle branch node, or glume/lemma dissection. All arrows are existing visible-only gross targets; no new microscopic anatomy claimed. See lane4_current_crew_gallery_reconciliation_20261026.
2026-10-27: Four exact research-grade Digitaria cognata individual-public-CC photograph originals physically archived with source, creator and EXIF-free JPEG. Physical blade/sheath free membrane remains an anatomy hold pending direct pixel inspection; no unverified arrows.
2026-10-27 actual saved image audit: 4 exact research-grade licensed *Digitaria cognata* green-grass source JPEGs physically installed. Two high-value true green leaf/sheath base panels selected and four arrows placed ONLY on visible exterior green leaf, sheath and pale torn sheath lip (actual free 0.5mm erose inner ligule unproven). Two lower-value crowded/duplicate angles kept as archive provenance, not promoted. Connected actual roots/attached flowering shoot and diffuse spikelet photos retained. Six photo roles [1,1,0.5,1,0.5,1]=5/6=83%.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Fall witchgrass — verify connected roots, truly airy panicle and photographed blade–sheath position
steps: START panels 1–2 (indices 0–1): original source-labelled Texas plants have a photographed perennial-looking rooted basal crown physically attached to narrow leaves and at least one wiry flowering head. Real attached fibrous roots are not guessed from soil shadows.

Panel 11 (index 10): Anne Parker's close CC BY image shows a pale split/torn OUTER sheath edge and a green narrow blade. This shows exactly where to look next, but the broken-looking flap has not been authenticated as an internal ligule or measured to 0.5mm. Do not arrow it as a ligule.
Panel 12 (index 11): source-labelled Georgia stem shows real exterior sheath and attached narrow leaf blades; no inward view of free membranous ligule.

Panels 4 and 6 (indices 3 and 5) document the actual wispy open panicle and separated oval spikelets on hair-thin branches; these contrast with *D. ciliaris* clustered fingerlike racemes in comparison panels 8–10 (indices 7–9).

Published Hill Country key: an erose membranous ligule about 0.5 mm is expected, but NONE of the archived photos clearly shows that actual distinct inner free ligule at scale. Photograph an OPENED sheath from the inside under 10x–40x beside a 1-mm bar to finish this role.

Need a clear genuine swollen fine-branch axil with radiating hairs and separately exposed *D. cognata* lower and upper glumes, sterile lemma, fertile lemma and palea under 1-mm graduated scale. None can be inferred from the seedhead silhouette.
Two additional research-grade CC BY original JPEGs are locally archived as provenance; crowded foliage/basal tuft without visible true inner membrane are withheld from ordinary field teaching panels.
Source native Texas at state level does NOT automatically establish Hays BONAP county occurrence. Preserve the original county range caution.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: First find the true extremely OPEN branching panicle (unlike Digitaria ciliaris fingerlike racemes), verify an actually connected rooted base and flowering culm, then inspect the INNER ~0.5-mm erose membranous ligule. The pictured split OUTER sheath edge is not enough.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: 11 source species photographs physically in GitHub; 12 field teaching panels (9 actual species panels +3 unmistakably other-taxon southern crabgrass look-alikes); four new anatomy gross pointers. Conservative photographic six-role=5/6=83%: roots, habit, real separate spikelets and lookalike contrast established, but free inner ligule, glume/lemma microdissection and hairy branch-axil macro still missing. No Hays county native reclassification.

what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: In-situ rooted Hays-area specimen showing complete attached flowering culm and habitat (an extracted rooted specimen with connected fibrous roots is already photographed in existing panels 1–2)
True inner membranous ligule at opened sheath–blade junction with 1-mm scale, not outer collar hairs/auricle lobe
Macro at 10–20× of truly swollen flowering branch axil with visible radiating hairs
Two opposing margins of the SAME leaf with 1-mm scale, documenting pale uneven/crimped edge
Three mature oval spikelets and distinct lower/upper glumes and lower sterile/upper fertile lemmas with 1-mm reference

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — AIRY TUMBLING PANICLE
field_id_short_tiles.short: A wide, open, wiry broom with separate oval spikelets on fine stalks.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Actual full flowering architecture appears in D. cognata panels 2 and 4 (indices 1,3), with individual terminal spikelets in panels 6–7 (indices 5,6). The airy panicle is visible but alone cannot confirm a Hays County voucher or microscopic glume lengths.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · KNOTTY PERENNIAL BASE AND TRUE LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Perennial leafy crown; membranous ligule ~0.2–1.5 mm (often ~0.5 mm in Texas key).
field_id_short_tiles.details: Panels 1–2 (indices 0–1) now show a source-identified collected whole plant with attached fibrous roots, leafy basal tillers and wiry flowering culm. At the leaf blade–sheath junction, however, the true free inner membrane has NOT been exposed and measured; a sheath surface is not the ligule. Panel 3 (index 2) shows a pale uneven blade edge, not a measured same-leaf two-margin comparison. Some regional sources differ on auricle-like lobes; don't decide from these alone.
field_id_short_tiles.status: ROOTED BASE SHOWN — TRUE LIGULE PHOTO MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · MEASURE THE MATURE SPIKELET
field_id_short_tiles.short: Oval spikelets ~2.2–3.1 mm; solitary on slender pedicels.
field_id_short_tiles.details: D. cognata terminal spikelets are visibly spaced along hair-thin pedicels in panels 6–7 (indices 5–6). With no scale they cannot establish exact dimensions or separate glumes and lemmas. Collect 3–5 ripe spikelets from a botanically authenticated specimen and photograph with 1-mm reference; published range is about 2.2–3.1 mm.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · TWO GLUMES, TWO DIFFERENT FLORETS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Tiny lower glume ≤1 mm; upper glume ~1.8–2.8 mm, usually 3–5-veined.
field_id_short_tiles.details: A mature spikelet has a reduced lower glume, a much longer upper glume, one lower sterile floret with an approximately 7-veined lemma, and one upper fertile floret with lemma and palea. No long glume or lemma awns. Minnesota Wildflowers describes the upper glume as sometimes finely hairy between veins. Do not confuse the two FLORETS with two separate spikelets or label microscopic bracts in unresolvable gallery pixels.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · LOOK-ALIKES AND HAIR PLACEMENT
field_id_short_tiles.short: Not crabgrass fingers, not Panicum's annual habit, not lovegrass multiflowered spikelets.
field_id_short_tiles.details: D. ciliaris in the final three gallery panels 8–10 (indices 7–9) shows compact, one-sided fingerlike racemes and overlapping spikelets, unlike the dispersed units of D. cognata. Compare Panicum capillare (hair-fringe ligule, usually annual) and Eragrostis spectabilis (multifloret spikelets) from sources, not from these D. ciliaris images. Actual D. cognata swollen hairy branch axils and open inner ligule remain photographic gaps.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · PUBLIC-READY GATE
field_id_short_tiles.short: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS — don't certify county native status or microscopic completion.
field_id_short_tiles.details: CURRENT PHOTO EVIDENCE: seven physically archived D. cognata photographs in indices 0–6 show a dug-up connected fibrous-rooted crown and flowering culm (0–1), candidate pale uneven blade margin (2), airy panicle (3), basal tuft (4), and individual terminal spikelets (5–6). Three D. ciliaris look-alike panels occupy indices 7–9. These are 18 existing gross markers on the species and 8 on the different-species comparisons, NOT evidence of a measured ligule, hairy branch axil or dissected glumes. NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: opened ~0.2–1.5 mm true membranous ligule with 1-mm scale; swollen hairy flowering branch axil; opposing margins of same leaf; calibrated mature spikelets and glume/lemma/palea dissection; Hays-area in-situ rooted habitat specimen. NEEDS_SITE_QA: verify exact CC BY/CC0 credits, panel indices, arrows and rights-filtered mobile Pages deployment. Preserve Hays BONAP county-native hold.
field_id_short_tiles.status: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS — TRUE LIGULE AND MACRO ANATOMY NOT PHOTOGRAPHED

grass_finalization.run_scope: Existing canonical Digitaria cognata only; practical Central Texas field ID, not Hays native-range certification.
grass_finalization.LOOK_HERE_FIRST: Find a very airy, wire-fine branching panicle with individually stalked oval spikelets, not tightly packed fingerlike racemes. Trace the flowering culm to a perennial leafy crown, then inspect the true inner ligule and ripe spikelet.

measured_published_key.growth_form: Warm-season perennial with wiry culms and persistent knotty leafy base; existing collected source-labelled specimen physically shows connected fibrous roots, leafy tillers and attached flowering culm, not an in-situ Hays voucher.
measured_published_key.ligule: True inner membranous ligule approximately 0.2–1.5 mm (regional Texas key often ~0.5 mm); no currently archived calibrated inner free membrane view.
measured_published_key.panicle: Very open diffuse branching panicle; small oval spikelets individually situated on hair-thin pedicels. Hair-bearing swollen branch axils remain unverified in current pixels.
measured_published_key.spikelets: Mature oval awnless spikelets approximately 2.2–3.1 mm; unscaled gallery photos cannot verify length.
measured_published_key.glumes: Lower glume reduced, often ≤1 mm; upper glume ~1.8–2.8 mm, commonly 3–5-veined.
measured_published_key.lemmas: Lower sterile lemma roughly spikelet length and commonly about 7-veined; upper fertile lemma and palea firm, no long true awns. Dissection is missing.
measured_published_key.evidence_limit: Ranges from documented flora treatments; no new microscopic measurements from photo pixels. Historical Leptoloma cognatum name is synonym, not another installed card.

grass_finalization.lookalikes: D. ciliaris has several compact one-sided fingerlike racemes and crowded paired spikelets (gallery indices 7–9). Panicum capillare is generally annual and has a hair-fringed ligule; Eragrostis spectabilis has multiflowered spikelets. These other genera are text comparisons, not displayed in the current ten panels.
